notes: Shoulder-mount 4K XDCAM broadcast camcorder (2/3-type 3-chip CMOS, global shutter). Ports extracted from Sony's official Operating Instructions manual (Specifications section and connector description pages, as mirrored on ManualsLib) plus B&H/search-corroborated details. Network is 100BASE-TX/10BASE-T only per the manual, so no eth-1g grade applies (mapped to eth-100m). USB is 2x Type-A + 1x Type-B, 4-pin each; USB generation/speed is not stated in the manual (no SuperSpeed/3.0 marking found in the primary spec table), so grade is omitted rather than guessed — some third-party listings call the control ports \"USB 3.0\" but this was not confirmed on the authoritative connector spec page. LENS (12-pin), VIEWFINDER (round 20-pin), and WRR (D-sub 15-pin, for wireless mic receiver slot) are proprietary Sony connectors with no exact match in the allowed connector list; they are omitted from the port list rather than mis-mapped (closest analogues would be euroblock/rs232-class control, but that would misrepresent them). The LIGHT connector is a 2-pin accessory DC power output (D-tap-style); mapped to dc-barrel as the closest available connector id since no dedicated 2-pin accessory/D-tap id exists. SxS (x2) and SD (x2, Proxy/Utility) media card slots exist but are storage media slots, not cable/signal connectors, so they are excluded per the port schema's focus on physical signal/power I/O. HDMI/USB/Ethernet lack explicit version numbers in Sony's spec table, so no bandwidth grade was set for those (per instructions, grade omitted when spec doesn't state version/speed) except Ethernet where 100BASE-TX is explicitly stated (eth-100m).

ports.name: AUDIO OUT
ports.note: 5-pin male, +4/0/-3 dBu balanced; outputs CH1/2 or CH3/4

ports.note: 8-pin proprietary remote-control connector; closest listed connector family is serial control (rs232) — actual connector is a Sony 8-pin remote jack, not true RS-232 D-sub. Power must be off to connect/disconnect.

ports.name: DC IN
